title: US Spot XRP ETFs See Largest Weekly Outflows in 8 Months as XRP Falls Below $1
text:
US Spot XRP ETFs See Largest Weekly Outflows in 8 Months as XRP Falls Below $1| KuCoin US Spot XRP ETFs See Largest Weekly Outflows in 8 Months as XRP Falls Below $1 Home Blog Market Insight Details US Spot XRP ETFs See Largest Weekly Outflows in 8 Months as XRP Falls Below $1
 2026/11/17 15:44:00 
 U.S. spot XRP exchange-traded funds (ETFs) recorded  $19.13 million in net outflows during November 9–13, 2026 , marking their largest weekly withdrawal in eight months. The decline coincided with broader cryptocurrency market weakness, as XRP subsequently fell below the psychologically important $1 level. Grayscale and Bitwise accounted for most of the ETF withdrawals, while Franklin Templeton attracted fresh capital. Despite the negative flows, cumulative ETF inflows remain near $1.79 billion. The divergence between short-term redemptions and longer-term investment demand raises questions about institutional sentiment, market liquidity, and XRP's near-term outlook. 
 Key Takeaways
 U.S. spot XRP ETFs recorded $19.13 million in weekly net outflows during November 9–13, their largest weekly withdrawal since March 2026 and the second consecutive week of negative flows. 
 Grayscale's GXRP led redemptions with approximately $12.71 million , followed by Bitwise's XRP ETF with $9.40 million, while Franklin Templeton's XRPZ attracted $4.45 million. 
 Combined XRP ETF net assets fell approximately 14% to $1.15 billion , but most of the decline reflected falling asset valuations rather than investor withdrawals. 
 XRP slipped below $1 during the weekend following the reporting period , amid broader cryptocurrency weakness and deteriorating short-term market sentiment. 
 Cumulative ETF net inflows remain near $1.79 billion , indicating that the latest withdrawals represent a short-term reversal rather than evidence of a complete institutional exit. 
 What Happened to US Spot XRP ETFs in November 2026?
 U.S.-listed spot XRP ETFs experienced their largest weekly net withdrawal in eight months during the trading week ending November 13, 2026. According to SoSoValue data, the funds recorded approximately $19.13 million in aggregate net outflows, their second consecutive negative week. The withdrawal was the largest since March 2026 and ranked among the four biggest weekly outflow periods since U.S. spot XRP ETFs began launching in November 2025. The figures indicate weakening short-term demand through exchange-traded investment products, although they do not establish that investors are abandoning XRP as an asset. 
 The selling was heavily concentrated in the first two sessions. On November 9, U.S. spot XRP ETFs recorded approximately $10.42 million in net outflows, their largest daily withdrawal since early March. Another $7.62 million left on November 10, while November 11 and 12 showed no reported net changes. The week ended with an additional $1.09 million in withdrawals on November 13. Together, the first two trading days accounted for approximately 94% of the weekly net outflow, suggesting that the decline was driven by a relatively concentrated period of selling rather than five consecutive days of substantial redemptions.

 The latest figures are notable because the products had previously accumulated substantial investment demand. Combined cumulative net inflows remained near $1.79 billion as of November 13, while total net assets stood at approximately $1.15 billion. The contrast highlights why short-term ETF flows and cumulative investor demand must be assessed separately . Weekly redemptions reveal a recent shift in positioning, whereas cumulative flows capture the longer history of subscriptions and withdrawals since the products launched. 
 Which XRP ETFs Recorded the Largest Outflows?
 The weekly withdrawals were not evenly distributed across U.S. spot XRP ETFs. Grayscale XRP Trust (GXRP) experienced approximately $12.71 million in net outflows, making it the largest contributor to the market-wide decline. Bitwise's XRP ETF followed with approximately $9.40 million in withdrawals. Together, these two products recorded more than $22 million in gross negative net flows, exceeding the aggregate market withdrawal because inflows into another fund partially offset their losses. 
 Canary's XRPC and 21Shares' TOXR also registered comparatively modest outflows, while Franklin Templeton's XRPZ attracted approximately $4.45 million in net inflows. This divergence is important because it demonstrates that investors were not uniformly reducing their exposure through every XRP ETF. Fund-specific demand may reflect differences in trading liquidity, expense ratios, institutional distribution arrangements, tax considerations, or portfolio allocation preferences, although the available flow data cannot determine which factors motivated individual investors.

 The different results also raise the possibility of investors changing their preferred ETF products rather than exiting XRP exposure altogether. For example, an investor could redeem shares from one issuer and purchase shares from another because of differences in fees or execution costs. However, Franklin's inflows cannot be directly attributed to withdrawals from Grayscale or Bitwise without evidence tracing the underlying transactions. A single week of divergent flows is insufficient to establish a lasting shift in market share or institutional preferences. 
 Why Are Investors Pulling Money From XRP ETFs?
 The immediate drivers of XRP ETF redemptions cannot be established from fund-flow data alone. Nevertheless, several market conditions may help explain why investors reduced exposure during the reporting period. The withdrawals occurred alongside broader weakness in digital assets, including Bitcoin (BTC) and Ethereum (ETH), suggesting that declining risk appetite was not confined to XRP. During the week ending November 13, XRP lost approximately 14.3%, compared with declines of roughly 9.9% for Bitcoin and 13.8% for Ethereum, according to contemporaneous market data. 
 When cryptocurrency prices fall sharply, investors may reduce positions to manage volatility, meet portfolio risk limits, or rebalance allocations. Spot ETFs provide an accessible way to adjust exposure without directly holding digital assets, making them a potential channel for institutional and brokerage-account withdrawals. However, weaker ETF flows can be both a response to falling prices and an additional source of selling pressure. The direction of causality cannot be established simply because redemptions and price declines occur during the same period. 
 Broader financial conditions may also influence investment demand. Changes in U.S. Treasury yields, Federal Reserve policy expectations, and equity-market volatility can affect the willingness of investors to hold higher-risk assets. XRP is additionally exposed to developments involving the XRP Ledger, Ripple-related business activity, and digital asset regulation. The asset itself is distinct from Ripple, the private company associated with parts of its ecosystem, as explained in the underlying characteristics of XRP and the XRP Ledger . 
 The distribution of withdrawals across individual ETF issuers suggests that product-level considerations may also be relevant. Institutional accounts can differ in their approved investment vehicles, trading requirements, custody arrangements, and transaction costs. Changes in these preferences may create outflows from one fund even while another receives subscriptions. Consequently, the November figures are best interpreted as evidence of weaker aggregate ETF demand combined with uneven investor positioning , rather than proof of a single coordinated institutional decision to sell XRP. 
 Why Did XRP ETF Assets Fall 14% When Net Outflows Were Only $19.13 Million?
 One of the most significant details in the latest XRP ETF data is the difference between net investor withdrawals and the decline in assets under management (AUM). Combined U.S. spot XRP ETF net assets reportedly decreased from approximately $1.34 billion to $1.15 billion during the week, a reduction of about $191 million, or 14%. Yet net withdrawals amounted to only $19.13 million. The much larger reduction in asset value indicates that changes in the market price of XRP , rather than redemptions alone, accounted for most of the reported decline. 
 ETF net flows measure net subscriptions and redemptions, while AUM measures the current market value of assets held by the funds after accounting for relevant assets and liabilities. If an ETF holds XRP and the cryptocurrency's price declines, the value of its holdings falls even when the number of shares outstanding remains unchanged. Conversely, AUM can rise because of XRP price appreciation without equivalent new investor deposits.

 A simplified comparison shows that the $19.13 million weekly outflow represented approximately 10% of the reported $191 million decline in combined net assets. The remaining difference largely reflects changing market valuations, although cash balances, fund expenses, settlement timing, and reporting methodologies can also affect the precise reconciliation. It would therefore be inaccurate to describe the full $191 million AUM decrease as money withdrawn by ETF investors. 
 The relationship between cumulative inflows and current assets can also appear counterintuitive. Although XRP ETFs have recorded approximately $1.79 billion in cumulative net inflows, their combined net assets were lower at $1.15 billion. These figures are not contradictory: cumulative flows reflect historical transactions, whereas AUM reflects current valuations. A fund can retain substantial cumulative inflows while holding assets worth considerably less after a prolonged decline in the underlying cryptocurrency. 
 How Are XRP ETF Outflows Affecting the XRP Price?
 XRP's decline below $1 intensified attention on the ETF withdrawals, but the timing requires careful interpretation. The $19.13 million weekly flow figure covers U.S. trading sessions through Friday, November 13, while reports of XRP breaking below $1 primarily concern trading during the following weekend. XRP subsequently approached $0.90 on November 14, its weakest reported level since November 2024, before trading around $0.95 in November 16 market coverage. These prices illustrate the broader market weakness accompanying the ETF developments, not a proven direct effect of the redemptions. 
 The $1 threshold is significant largely because it represents a widely watched psychological price level. When an asset trades near a round number, some market participants may cluster stop-loss orders, take-profit instructions, or leveraged positions around that level. A break below it can coincide with additional volatility, particularly when order-book depth is limited. However, a psychological threshold is not a guaranteed technical support level, and trading below $1 does not independently establish that further losses will follow. 
 The potential relationship between ETF redemptions and spot prices also depends on fund mechanics. Shares of a spot XRP ETF trade between buyers and sellers in the secondary market, while authorized participants and other market intermediaries facilitate the creation and redemption of fund shares under the applicable structure. Ordinary trading of existing ETF shares does not necessarily trigger an equivalent immediate transaction in XRP itself. Actual pressure on the underlying asset depends on fund-level creations or redemptions, inventory management, and market execution conditions. 
 Conclusion
 The $19.13 million weekly outflow from U.S. spot XRP ETFs marks a significant reversal in short-term investment demand, particularly as XRP has fallen below $1. However, the headline figure requires context: most of the 14% decline in ETF net assets reflects market valuation changes rather than investor withdrawals, and cumulative inflows remain near $1.79 billion. Divergent performance across Grayscale, Bitwise, and Franklin Templeton further suggests that demand is not uniform. Whether the latest weakness persists will depend on future ETF flows, XRP price behavior, market liquidity, and broader cryptocurrency conditions rather than one week's redemptions alone. 
 FAQs
 What Does an XRP ETF Net Outflow Mean?
 An XRP ETF net outflow occurs when the value of fund share redemptions exceeds new creations over a reporting period. It indicates a net reduction in investor exposure through the ETF structure, although it does not necessarily represent an immediate, equivalent sale of XRP in the spot market. 
 Do Spot XRP ETFs Hold XRP Directly?
 Spot XRP ETFs are designed to provide exposure to the underlying cryptocurrency and generally hold XRP through approved custody arrangements. Their structures differ from futures-based products, which obtain exposure through derivative contracts. Investors should review each fund's prospectus for its specific holdings and redemption procedures. 
 Can XRP Recover While ETFs Continue to Record Outflows?
 Yes. XRP prices can rise despite ETF withdrawals if buying demand from exchanges, other institutional investors, or broader cryptocurrency markets outweighs selling pressure. ETF flows are one indicator of demand, but they do not represent every transaction or participant in the XRP market. 
 Does Falling XRP ETF AUM Always Mean Investors Are Selling?
 No. ETF assets under management can decline when XRP prices fall, even without substantial net redemptions. AUM reflects the market value of fund holdings, while net flows measure subscriptions and withdrawals. Both indicators are needed to evaluate changes in investor activity accurately.
